fieldMarks: Moderate-sized lizard with a tail more than twice the length of the rest of the body and a relatively large head (NDOW).
Small scales over the whole body; white, gray or cream with darker spots on the back and legs (NDOW).
Breeding females develop bright orange spots along the sides (NDOW).
behavior: Mostly ground-dwelling; when threatened runs to the base of a shrub and freezes (NDOW; NatureServe).
Not territorial; adults largely ignore each other except when mating (NDOW).
Eats insects, spiders, lizards, snakes, small rodents and some plant material, and can eat a lizard nearly its own size (NDOW).
Active about May-August in the north and late March or April to late summer or fall in the south; animals active in late summer are mostly hatchlings (NatureServe).
habitat: Sandy and rocky desert and semidesert with scattered low shrubs (creosotebush, sagebrush), especially areas with many rodent burrows; avoids dense vegetation (NDOW; NatureServe).
range: Oregon, southern Idaho, Utah and western Colorado south through eastern and southern California, Nevada, Arizona, New Mexico and western Texas to northeastern Baja California and north-central mainland Mexico (NatureServe).
